links.outcome: Proportion of oncologists with formal AI training
links.effect: 88% (95% CI 70.0-95.8) of 25 respondents had no formal AI training, while all had used LLMs and 20% used them for clinical decision support.
links.quote: In total 25 physicians responded (59.5%), 88% (95% CI 70.0-95.8) of whom had no formal AI training.

links.outcome: Physician perception of who bears legal responsibility for AI-related errors
links.effect: 88% (70.0-95.8) of physicians perceived they would bear primarily legal responsibility for AI errors; 64% (44.5-79.8) cited regulatory/legal uncertainty as a barrier.
links.quote: Most participants (84%; 65.3-93.6) supported the use of AI as a clinical decision-support tool, yet 88% (70.0-95.8) of physicians perceived they would bear primarily legal responsibility for AI-related errors.

screen.reason: National cross-sectional survey of oncologists assessing knowledge, attitudes, real-world professional use, and barriers regarding AI/LLMs in oncology practice.
